{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# flux batch script
#
# Resource requests translated from Slurm:
#   -N 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=4  => 4 MPI ranks total
#   --cpus-per-task=7    => 7 cores per rank
#   --gres=gpu:4         => 4 GPUs
#   -t 24:00:00
#
# NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-socket=2 has no direct Flux portable batch equivalent here.
# Omitting it may reduce performance due to different rank/core placement across sockets.
#
# NOTE: Slurm mail notifications (--mail-type/--mail-user) are not translated.
# Omitting them has no runtime performance impact, but you will not get email on start/end.
#
# NOTE: The Slurm line "# SBATCH --mem=32G" is commented out in the input; no memory request is made.

flux batch \
  -N 1 \
  -n 4 \
  -c 7 \
  -g 4 \
  -t 24h \
  --wrap 'set -e

# load environment
module load cudatoolkit/10.0
module load cudnn/cuda-10.0/7.6.3
module load openmpi/gcc/3.1.3/64
#module load fftw
source /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/tensorflow-venv/bin/activate
module load /home/tgartner/modulefiles/plumed-tg
# export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

if [ -f "Sampledone.txt" ]; then
    echo "Simulation finished"
elif ! grep -q "ERROR" slurm*; then
    echo "Continuing NPT sampling"
    # Slurm-specific self-resubmission via sbatch --dependency is omitted.
    # Omitting it may reduce throughput/automation because the follow-on job will not be queued automatically.

    # run NPT sampling
    # Use Flux launcher instead of mpirun to respect Flux resource allocation.
    flux run -n 4 -c 7 -g 4 /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/lammps-3Mar20/src/lmp_mpi -i in.lammps.sample -e screen
else
    echo "There is an error"
fi'
"
}

    "Inside the wrapped payload, `flux run -g 4` assumes per-task GPU allocation semantics that match your Flux configuration; misconfiguration can cause runtime placement/allocation issues."
  ]
}

# NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-socket=2 has no direct Flux batch directive equivalent here.
# Omitting it may reduce performance due to different rank/core placement across sockets.
#
# NOTE: Slurm mail notifications (--mail-type/--mail-user) are not translated.
# Omitting them has no runtime performance impact, but you will not get email on start/end.
#
# NOTE: The Slurm line "# SBATCH --mem=32G" is commented out in the input; no memory request is made.

set -e

# load environment
module load cudatoolkit/10.0
module load cudnn/cuda-10.0/7.6.3
module load openmpi/gcc/3.1.3/64
#module load fftw
source /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/tensorflow-venv/bin/activate
module load /home/tgartner/modulefiles/plumed-tg
# export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

if [ -f "Sampledone.txt" ]; then
    echo "Simulation finished"
elif ! grep -q 'ERROR' slurm*; then
    echo "Continuing NPT sampling"

    # Slurm-specific self-resubmission via sbatch --dependency has no direct Flux equivalent here.
    # Omitting it may reduce throughput/automation because the follow-on job will not be queued automatically.

    # run NPT sampling
    # Use Flux launcher instead of mpirun to respect Flux resource allocation.
    flux run -n 4 -c 7 -g 4 /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/lammps-3Mar20/src/lmp_mpi -i in.lammps.sample -e screen
else
    echo "There is an error"
fi

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -N 1   # node count
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-socket=2
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=7
#SBATCH -t 24:00:00
# SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:4
#SBATCH --mail-type=begin
#SBATCH --mail-type=end
#SBATCH --mail-user=tgartner@princeton.edu

# load environment
module load cudatoolkit/10.0
module load cudnn/cuda-10.0/7.6.3
module load openmpi/gcc/3.1.3/64
#module load fftw
source /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/tensorflow-venv/bin/activate
module load /home/tgartner/modulefiles/plumed-tg
# export OMP_NUM_THREADS=1

if [ -f "Sampledone.txt" ]; then
    echo "Simulation finished"
elif ! grep -q 'ERROR' slurm*; then
    echo "Continuing NPT sampling"
    sbatch --dependency=afterany:$SLURM_JOB_ID run.sample.qs
    # run NPT sampling
    mpirun /home/tgartner/Software-deepmd-kit-1.0/lammps-3Mar20/src/lmp_mpi -i in.lammps.sample -e screen
else
    echo "There is an error"
fi
